strategies.overview: Regidrago's access to Dragon Energy paired with its decent Speed and monstrous HP allows it to be a great sweeper late-game while still having utility as a revenge killer mid-game. Regidrago's ability, Dragon's Maw, is amazing, strengthening its already powerful STAB Dragon Energy even further so that it OHKOes threats like Terrakion, Armarouge, and Basculegion-F. While Regidrago has enormous HP and its typing has many useful resistances, aiding it against Pokemon like Volcanion, Raikou, and Armarouge, it can't put either of them to good use, as it needs to conserve its HP to ensure Dragon Energy stays as strong as possible. Additionally, Regidrago's lack of coverage moves forces it to rely on Terastallization to even hit most Fairy-types for good damage. Regidrago is quite slow for a Choice Scarf user, too, underspeeding the majority of Choice Scarf foes such as Jirachi, Krookodile, Galarian Zapdos, and Gengar.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Pulse provides Regidrago with a reliable STAB move that it can use repeatedly, though it is weaker than Draco Meteor and—depending on Regidrago's current HP—Dragon Energy. Regidrago can run Choice Specs instead of Choice Scarf to more easily break through bulkier teams; however, Dragon Energy is typically powerful enough without any further boosts, and Choice Specs leaves Regidrago open to being revenge killed or taking damage much more easily. Regidrago can become a setup sweeper with Loaded Dice and a set of Dragon Dance / Scale Shot / Earthquake / Tera Blast Steel, capitalizing on its gargantuan HP to find multiple turns to set up, but it's quite reliant on Terastallization to get past certain Fairy-types like Air Balloon Klefki.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Regidrago's most powerful moves, Dragon Energy and Draco Meteor, are both entirely useless against Fairy-type Pokemon like Gardevoir, Air Balloon Klefki, and Mimikyu. Additionally, Air Balloon Klefki is immune to Earth Power, forcing Regidrago to either use Tera Blast Steel to hit it or switch out. Not only that, but Mimikyu's Disguise gives it insurance against Regidrago, protecting Mimikyu even if Regidrago goes for a coverage move. However, the majority of them need to watch out for Tera Blast Steel.

Steel-types: Specially defensive Steel-types such as Jirachi, Empoleon, Registeel, and Magnezone cause the most issues for Regidrago, since they can switch in and set up entry hazards in front of it.

Priority and Faster Choice Scarf Users: Due to Dragon Energy's power being heavily dependent on Regidrago's HP, Regidrago hates anything that could make it take damage before it attacks. For this reason, it's highly susceptible to Bisharp's Sucker Punch and especially Mamoswine's Ice Shard as well as common Choice Scarf foes such as Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, Gengar, and Mienshao.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Set Details

Regidrago is a threatening late-game sweeper, with its powerful Dragon Energy cleanly OHKOing many offensive foes such as Krookodile, Galarian Zapdos, and Feraligatr. However, Dragon Energy can be unreliable at times due to its insistence on Regidrago maintaining high HP. Draco Meteor provides a consistently strong attack regardless of Regidrago's current HP, though it's not as spammable as Dragon Energy due to its Special Attack-dropping effect. Earth Power complements Regidrago's Dragon-type STAB moves nicely, hitting Steel-types like Jirachi, Magnezone, and Empoleon super effectively. Similarly, Tera Blast Steel targets Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Mimikyu, which Regidrago immensely struggles against. Additionally, Tera Steel allows Regidrago to take on Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type attacks in a pinch from Pokemon like Gardevoir, Hisuian Goodra, and Mamoswine.

Regidrago thrives on balance and bulky offense structures that can keep it healthy through providing entry hazard control as well as switch-ins to faster threats while being able to chip its checks to open it up for a sweep late-game. Fairy-types like Gardevoir, Klefki, and Mimikyu are Regidrago's biggest roadblock to sweeping teams. Because of this, Regidrago greatly appreciates support from Steel-type partners that can handle them with ease, such as Bisharp, Registeel, Jirachi, and Magnezone. However, when these same Steel-type Pokemon are on the opposing team, they can cause problems for Regidrago. This means Magnezone is an especially good teammate, since it can provide extra support through Magnet Pull, locking in and KOing pesky opposing Steel-types for Regidrago. Additionally, other Pokemon that beat Steel-types like Krookodile, Mienshao, and Volcanion work well alongside Regidrago. What's more, Krookodile can surprise Fairy-types with its Gunk Shot; Mienshao is great at chipping and crippling Fairy-types with its U-turn and Knock Off, respectively; and Volcanion acts as a decent defensive switch-in to Fairy-types for Regidrago. Since Regidrago's chance at a sweep is heavily reliant on its ability to repeatedly throw off a powerful Dragon Energy, hazard control is vital. Defoggers like Talonflame complement Regidrago quite well, being decent switch-ins to Fairy-types like Gardevoir and Mimikyu while not overlapping with its typing unlike other hazard clearers such as Cyclizar and Noivern. In a similar vein, Wish passers and Healing Wish users like Umbreon, Jirachi, and Gardevoir as well as Lunar Dance Cresselia are great at keeping Regidrago healthy. Pivots like Magnezone, Galarian Zapdos, and Talonflame synergize well alongside Regidrago, as they can provide it with safe entry through their pivot moves, simultaneously keeping it healthy and maintaining Dragon Energy's power. On top of that, these three partners can threaten bothersome foes like Gardevoir, Registeel, and Mimikyu, respectively. Another issue with Regidrago is that the majority of Choice Scarf users outspeed Regidrago and, by dealing damage to it, threaten its chance at sweeping with Dragon Energy. This means that answers such as Slowbro and Gastrodon to Choice Scarf foes like Jirachi, Galarian Zapdos, and Krookodile are recommended. Pokemon like Klefki, Empoleon, and Rhyperior make for especially strong partners, as their hazards can wear down the opposing team to the point where Regidrago can sweep it without issue.

strategies.outdated: This analysis was uploaded prior to The Indigo Disk release and may contain outdated information.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Modest nature guarantees the 2HKO on Corviknight with Dragon Energy.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

movesets.name: Dragon Energy
movesets.description:
• With Draco Plate and Dragon's Maw, Regidrago's Dragon Energy hits most of the metagame for incredibly high neutral spread damage, offering great sweeping opportunities and removing important threats for its teammates.
  • Draco Meteor gives Regidrago an option when not at full HP, and being a single-target move, it offers an even higher damage output.
  • Earth Power, while often not getting 2HKOs, hits the Pokemon that resist Dragon Energy like Diancie and Gholdengo.
  • Tera Dragon helps Dragon Energy pick up KOs, notably getting the OHKO on bulky Ogerpon-W, while Tera Steel gives Regidrago resistances to a lot of common moves like Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm and Gholdengo's Make It Rain and also improves the matchup against Chien-Pao + Dragonite by letting it resist Extreme Speed and Ice Spinner.
  • Due to its middling Speed, Regidrago heavily relies on Tornadus's Tailwind support to hit first while being healthy and get maximum value from Dragon Energy. Tornadus can also use Icy Wind for additional speed control.
  • Regidrago greatly appreciates Pokemon that can strongly hit opposing targets that resist Dragon Energy, like Gholdengo and Diancie, in return for its ability to blow through Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Incineroar. Gholdengo can deal with Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and with Pokemon like Raging Bolt that often Terastallize into the Fairy typing to not get hit by Dragon-type moves. Ground-types like Landorus on Tailwind teams and Ursaluna-B on Trick Room teams are also great to remove Steel-types and Diancie.
  • Ogerpon-H is one of the main beneficiaries of Regidrago's ability to remove Fire-types, in return removing Steel-types, improving the snow matchup, and offering Follow Me support to help Regidrago dodge Sucker Punch and keep itself healthy. Ogerpon-W can also be an option that offers more reliable Follow Me support on defensive teams.
  • Regidrago is often paired with Farigiraf or Indeedee-F, which disincentivizes priority moves like Fake Out and Sucker Punch, and they can use Trick Room against Tailwind users or to reverse Trick Room from opposing users.

strategies.overview:
*Regidrago is a great offensive Pokemon that has immense damage output and can sweep teams easily thanks to Dragon's Maw and Dragon Energy.

*When paired with Pokemon like Tornadus, the Ogerpon formes, and Indeedee that provide speed control, redirection, and priority immunity, respectively, it truly becomes difficult to hinder Regidrago's damage output. Gholdengo is one of its best partners, as it can effectively remove Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao, which are major threats for Regidrago.

*Regidrago cannot damage the most influential Pokemon of the format — Flutter Mane—with its STAB moves. Its middling Speed makes it vulnerable to faster threats, though with the right support that ensures that all the Fairy-, Steel-types, and common Focus Sash users like Chien-Pao are checked, it can absolutely steamroll teams.

movesets.name: Dragon Fang
movesets.description:
*Draco Meteor allows Regidrago to pick OHKOs when Dragon Energy isn't dealing much damage at low HP, and Earth Power allows it to damage to Steel types like Gholdengo and Kingambit.

*Regidrago boosts its damage output with Dragon Fang that stacks on Dragon Maw and does insane damage.

*Tera Steel is a great defensive Tera that allows it to resist its original weaknesses.

movesets.name: Three Attacks
movesets.description:
Regidrago is an offensive threat with great damage potential thanks to the combination of Dragon's Maw and its amazing Dragon-type STAB options. Draco Meteor gives Regidrago a powerful single-target burst option, being able to do massive damage to a majority of the format. While Dragon Pulse is weaker, it deals consistent damage over time, making it better for situations where the power of Draco Meteor is not necessary. Earth Power brings solid coverage into Regidrago's moveset for opposing Steel-types at the cost of not doing great damage due to it not being STAB- or Dragon's Maw-boosted. Tera Blast pairs well with Tera Ghost to threaten Ghost-weak Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Gholdengo. Life Orb helps increase Regidrago's damage output to insane levels, with the drawback of making Dragon Energy weaker over time; Dragon Fang, on the other hand, sacrifices higher damage output for the lack of recoil, giving Regidrago's Dragon Energy and bulk more consistency. Tera Dragon pushes Regidrago's damage even further, allowing it to pick up KOs on extremely bulky Pokemon like Calyrex-I with Draco Meteor and Helping Hand-boosted Dragon Energy, as well as Amoonguss and Incineroar with Tera Dragon Dragon Energy. Tera Ghost provides Regidrago with a Fake Out immunity, helping in its hyper-aggressive gameplan; it also has the extra benefit of removing its weaknesses.

Regidrago's biggest weakness is Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Zacian-C, as well as Tera Fairy Pokemon like Calyrex-S and Raging Bolt. Faster Pokemon like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Chien-Pao are other huge threats for Regidrago because they can outspeed and OHKO it. Zacian-C is a great partner for Regidrago, utilizing its typing to threaten Fairy-types. Terapagos is another good partner Restricted Pokemon, being an alternative spread move attacker that can punish opposing Tera Fairy Pokemon that Regidrago would struggle against. Tailwind setters like Tornadus and Whimsicott cover for Regidrago's middling Speed tier and provide it with the ability to outspeed faster threats, drastically increasing its snowball potential. Indeedee-F and Farigiraf are other great partners, blocking priority moves like Fake Out and Sucker Punch with their abilities, setting up Trick Room to help against certain matchups like opposing Tailwind teams, and using Helping Hand to make Regidrago stronger. Indeedee-F is especially helpful thanks to its access to Follow Me, providing redirection support for Regidrago.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Regidrago's massive HP stat, great offensive ability in Dragon's Maw, and passable dual offenses may make it an enticing Dragon-type wallbreaker addition to a draft. However, paper-thin defenses and the lack of reliable recovery blunt the effectiveness of an incredible base 200 HP, and a base 80 Speed makes it difficult for Regidrago to trade evenly with an opposing team, often needing to take hits while setting up or trying to take KOs. While Regidrago can play both an offensive and defensive role on a draft, it finds itself outclassed in its cost bracket when teams need only specifically one or the other. It gets completely walled by Fairy-types and many Steel-types, lacking coverage that can do meaningful damage unless it is made a Tera Captain, making it near impossible to bring to most matchups due to the prevalence of these Pokemon.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Choice Item Wallbreaker: Whether it's using a Choice Scarf to patch up its Speed or one of the offensive Choice items to provide more bite to an otherwise unremarkable base 100 attacking stat, Regidrago can serve as a hammer, bashing dents and holes into an opposing team until a teammate can come in for the sweep. Dragon Energy works particularly well on these sets early-game, especially when paired with teammates that can beat opposing Fairy-types.

Dragon Dance Sweeper: With so few things able to OHKO Regidrago, it can run Dragon Dance and attempt to sweep late-game. After a boost and the removal of Choice Scarf users, Regidrago can do significant damage to anything already chipped by its teammates.

Dual Screens Setter: With the difficulty of 2HKOing Regidrago, it can provide Light Screen and Reflect to its team, either switching out to attempt to do so again later or keeping momentum up with Explosion to bring in a teammate to set up. With the limited moveslot space, however, Regidrago cannot both set the screens and make use of them by setting up itself.

Wall: Despite a lack of recovery outside of Rest, an invested Regidrago can effectively sponge hits from powerful attackers thanks to its HP stat and large selection of useful resistances.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Dragon Energy, Draco Meteor, Outrage, Dragon Pulse, Dragon Claw

Setup Moves: Dragon Dance, Scale Shot

Utility Moves: Substitute, Light Screen, Reflect

Coverage: Crunch, Earth Power, Earthquake, Fire Fang, Hammer Arm, Ice Fang, Tera Blast, Thunder Fang

Niche Moves

Explosion: Explosion is an option to deal a large amount of damage while also allowing a teammate to come in and pick up the momentum created by Regidrago's sacrifice.

Rest and Sleep Talk: Regidrago's only healing option, Rest, allows it to maintain longevity, while Sleep Talk avoids the passivity associated with Rest. Chesto Berry can be used alongside Rest to serve as a one-time full heal.

Common Items

Sitrus Berry: With a sky-high HP stat, Sitrus Berry can provide it with a large amount of healing, allowing it to remain in play for longer.

Choice Band / Choice Specs: The two offense-boosting Choice items can turn a respectable, if underwhelming, offensive Regidrago into something that can dismantle the defensive backbone of an opposing team, especially if any opposing Fairy-type Pokemon have taken reasonable amounts of damage from teammates or its coverage.

Choice Scarf: With a Choice Scarf, Regidrago can outspeed most unboosted Pokemon, dispatching them with a powerful STAB Dragon Energy or a super effective coverage move.

Light Clay: Should Regidrago attempt a utility-focused dual screens setup role, the lack of a necessary item allows it to run Light Clay effectively, increasing the utility it provides with Light Screen and Reflect.

Heavy-Duty Boots: With Regidrago wanting to switch in multiple times during a game to check threats or deal damage, avoiding the chip from hazards is beneficial to its longevity.

Niche Items

Resist Berries: Regidrago can use resistance Berries such as the Haban and Yache Berries to potentially lure and remove a dangerous foe.

Rocky Helmet: Against physical wallbreakers, Regidrago can rely on a large HP value to tank multi-hit and pivoting contact moves, returning the damage in turn.

Loaded Dice: If Scale Shot is Regidrago's boosting move of choice, Loaded Dice increases the consistency and effectiveness of Scale Shot.

Eject Button / Red Card: With the ability to take hits, Regidrago can serve as either a pivot option, safely bringing in allies unscathed, or an emergency stop to an ascending sweeper.

Chesto Berry: Without reliable healing, Regidrago needs to rely on Rest to heal itself up, and it can use Chesto Berry to limit the negative side effects of Rest for one use.

Tera

Regidrago is not the best user of Terastallization, though it does not entirely waste it, either. Using Tera Dragon can allow it to pull additional damage out of its STAB options, while other Tera types can make it difficult to counter or allow it to defensively check a threatening foe. Tera Steel specifically can be used to gain an upper hand against Fairy- and Ice-types that may be tasked with its removal, while Tera Poison works well as another defensive option that can target Fairy-types. With stronger coverage thanks to Tera Blast, Dragon Dance sets can more reliably muscle through their counters.

Draft Strategy

Regidrago is a multi-faceted tool that, while not always effective, can provide a secondary or tertiary option for teams in defensive, offensive, and utility roles. When it's evaluated individually in any of those roles, Regidrago is unlikely the best option on a draft board for its price range, but its ability to serviceably handle multiple roles allows it to help teams in need of flexibility. It should not be the star of the show, though it does appreciate certain other tools being present.

Entry Hazard Control: Unable to avoid any hazards itself and always appreciative of the chip damage on its foes to secure KOs, Regidrago strongly enjoys having an advantage in the hazard game. Corviknight, Galarian Weezing, and Great Tusk can all bring Defog or Rapid Spin to the table, while Klefki, Landorus-T, and Gliscor can provide Spikes, Stealth Rocks, or both.

Offensive Poison- and Steel-types: Regidrago appreciates teammates that can threaten the Fairy- and Steel-types that block it from making progress. Pokemon like Sneasler and Gholdengo can provide Regidrago with a way around its most prescient threats.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Without coverage to hit them super effectively, Fairy-types like Iron Valiant or Clefable are the one stop shops to countering Regidrago, disabling its powerful STAB options and threatening back with super effective STAB options of their own.

Fast Wallbreakers: With Choice Scarf users potentially overcoming even boosted Regidrago and most Pokemon being faster than it naturally, a weakened Regidrago can be KOed by anything able to hit with a strong enough neutral hit. Few things can outright KO Regidrago, let alone without a super effective STAB option, but Regidrago's defenses can only go so far once it has been sufficiently damaged.

Chip Damage: Regidrago's health is not infinite and lacks recovery outside of Rest, so switching into entry hazards and pivoting moves or taking status ailments can quickly whittle away at Regidrago, making it much harder for it to effectively sponge actual hits.

Bulky Steel-types: Without a standout offensive stat, many Steel-types like Corviknight and Jirachi are able to stomach Regidrago's hits even if they mispredict the attacking stat of choice. Bulky Steel-types like Jirachi can even successfully take Regidrago's Ground-type coverage well.
